- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early periods of the 30-day window.
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and then decline too sharply, missing sustained upward trends.
- After sharp spikes in true values (e.g., 36.62, 38.18), forecasts lag and fail to capture the continuation or magnitude.
- Model underreacts to recent low prices in history, failing to anticipate rebounds.
- Mean reversion is overemphasized — forecasts often revert too quickly to prior averages, missing volatility or breakout phases.
- Forecasts show persistent bias toward higher values, especially when true outcomes exhibit strong downward momentum.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are overly optimistic in the first 5–10 days, then overly pessimistic in the last 10–15 days.
